name: Linezolid
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Linezolid needs no dose change at any level of kidney function, because parent-drug levels are unchanged. Its two inactive metabolites accumulate in kidney impairment, and thrombocytopenia is reported more often in severe kidney impairment, so weekly blood counts matter. Hemodialysis removes about 30% of a dose; give it after the session.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses CrCl (mL/min) in its PK study; no dose bands.

hd.text: No dose change; give after hemodialysis, as about 30% of a dose is removed in a 3-hour session (label). Its two inactive metabolites accumulate as kidney function falls; their clinical significance is unknown, so weigh the risk. pd.text: No information on peritoneal dialysis (label). For PD-associated peritonitis (ISPD 2022, systemic): IV or oral 600 mg twice daily for 48 hours, then 300 mg twice daily (Table 6). Specialist input.

crrt.text: Not in label. Li 2020 (Table 3): no change in CVVH, CVVHD or CVVHDF; exposure varies widely, and Li suggests drug level monitoring.

dialyzable: Partly: about 30% of a dose removed in a 3-hour hemodialysis; both metabolites are also removed (label).
monitoring: Complete blood count weekly (more important in severe kidney impairment, courses over 2 weeks, or with myelosuppressive drugs); lactic acidosis; serotonin syndrome with serotonergic drugs; vision and neuropathy with courses over 28 days; blood glucose in diabetes; serum sodium (label).

pediatric.usual_dose: Preterm neonates (under 34 weeks' gestation) under 7 days: 10 mg/kg every 12 hours, increased to every 8 hours if response is poor; all neonates 10 mg/kg every 8 hours by 7 days of age (label). Birth to 11 years: 10 mg/kg IV or oral every 8 hours (uncomplicated skin infection: under 5 years every 8 hours, 5–11 years every 12 hours). 12 years and older: 600 mg every 12 hours (label).
